questions.question: Our network planning sheet needs a current leg total. How many shipment legs are recorded?
Some consignments travel on several legs. How many different consignments are represented in the current leg records?
For the current network activity, what is the total transported weight in kilograms?
How much has the current leg activity incurred in handling charges, expressed in US dollars?
What is the average recorded transit time, in minutes per leg, across the current records?
Prepare a customer-market breakdown of current handling charges and transported kilograms, with the largest charge total first.
For each customer market and destination zone together, report current handling charges and the number of distinct consignments; put the largest charges first.
Compare current service-class and carrier combinations using average transit minutes and leg count. Start with the shortest average, breaking ties alphabetically by service class and then carrier.
How are current legs distributed across shipment states? Keep unassigned states as a group and list the state labels alphabetically.
Give me the current transported kilograms month by month, starting with the earliest departure month.
For current legs whose service tariff is more than 1,800 cents, what are the average transit minutes and total handling charges?
Count the current legs whose whole-consignment charge is at least 20,000 cents but whose own handling charge is below 5,000 cents, and give their total handling charges in dollars.
In the Retail customer market, how many current legs carry exactly four packages?
What are the current transported weight and handling charges for Express or Overnight legs going to North or West destination zones, when route distance is at least 1,000 kilometers?
For current legs marked Delayed whose shipment state is Delivered, show the leg count and average transit minutes.
For active carriers, count current legs in every service class except Freight, split by carrier and listed alphabetically.
Which destination zones have more than 850,000 kilograms of current transported weight? Show each qualifying total, largest first.
Only consider current legs with a service tariff above 1,000 cents. Among their carriers, show those whose total handling charges exceed $73,000, highest total first.
List service classes represented by at least 2,000 distinct consignments in current legs, showing those distinct counts from highest to lowest.
How many current legs have at least one shipment-leg exception recorded?
For current legs with no recorded exceptions at all, give the transported weight and handling-charge totals.
How much handling charge did current legs incur when they had a Damage exception of severity at least 3? Also count those legs once each.
Count current legs for which no exception has been marked Resolved; legs without any exception should count too.
Give the current leg count and transported kilograms after excluding any leg with an Open Weather exception. Other exceptions may remain.
For active carriers, compare average transit minutes and leg counts among current legs with a Weather or Customs exception of severity at least 4. Put the longest average first.
Which customer markets have current handling-charge totals above the average of all customer-market totals? Show their totals, highest first.
Considering only current Express legs, show the two destination zones with the largest transported weights among zones above the average zone total for those Express legs.
Among current service-class and carrier pairs, show the four largest leg counts that exceed the average count across all pairs. Break count ties by service class, then carrier, alphabetically.
Append archived legs to current legs, retaining overlapping rows. How many leg records and distinct consignments does that combined population contain?
Combine current and archived legs but remove rows duplicated exactly across every approved leg column. Report the leg count and distinct consignment count.
Using current and archived legs with every overlap retained, show the five customer-market and destination-zone pairs with the largest handling-charge totals.
Make a departure-month series of transported kilograms across current and archived legs, dropping only exact duplicate leg rows. Start with the oldest month.
For last calendar month, what were the current handling charges and leg count?
For this month through the catalog reference date, give the transported weight and average transit minutes of current legs.
How many current legs departed on 2026-09-12 itself?
From 2026-06-01 through 2026-08-31 inclusive, show average transit minutes for current legs by departure month, in calendar order.
For current legs belonging to Cancelled shipments, what are the average transit minutes and the leg count?
Which three carrier groups have the fewest current legs? Show the counts from smallest to largest, including an unassigned carrier group if present, with alphabetical carrier ties.
For current legs with route distance greater than 999,999 kilometers, return total handling charges, leg count, and average transit minutes.
Using only current records, list handling charges for each customer market for departures from 2025-07-01 through 2025-07-31, highest charge first.
Export each recipient's full name, email address, phone number and street address for the current shipments.
For each carrier, divide total handling charges by transported kilograms and rank carriers by that cost per kilogram.
Show cumulative handling charges for current legs month by month, with each month including all earlier months.
Within every customer market, find the three largest individual leg handling charges and add only those three amounts into a market total.
How is our logistics performance looking overall?
Break down current handling charges by area, with the largest area first.
Count current legs where the destination zone is North or the customer market is Healthcare.
Show current leg counts for carriers whose names contain the word Air.
Give one leg-count total using current records only, and include every archived record in that same total.
Merge current and archived records, keep only the latest-departing leg for each consignment, then total its handling charges.
